title: Disentangling Multi-View Scanning in Mamba for Network Traffic Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Timely and accurate network traffic anomaly detection remains challenging.

gap.claim: Existing multi-view Mamba scanning can accumulate redundant view-invariant information, dilute or suppress view-specific information, and cause representation homogenization and multi-view degradation.

contributions.claim: DisenMamba is a disentangled multi-view Mamba framework for network traffic anomaly detection.
DisenMamba reformulates multi-view scanning as a two-stage disentangle-then-fuse process that separates view-invariant and view-specific components before fusion.
The authors provide code for DisenMamba.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DisenMamba as a novel framework and characterize the approach as establishing a new disentangled multi-view Mamba paradigm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of DisenMamba.
The authors report that the design yields more discriminative representations for subtle traffic anomalies.
Code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Network traffic anomaly detection is important but remains difficult to perform accurately and promptly.
Mamba is presented as a promising linear-time backbone, with multi-view scanning intended to provide complementary contextual cues.
The paper identifies redundancy accumulation in multi-view scanning, where invariant information is amplified and view-specific information is weakened.
DisenMamba separates invariant and specific components before fusion through a two-stage disentangle-then-fuse process.
The authors report improved discriminative representations and experimental effectiveness, while describing the work as a new paradigm.

source_observation.claim: Multi-view fusion can repeatedly amplify shared information while weakening information specific to individual views.

interpretation.claim: Separating shared and view-specific components before fusion may reduce redundancy and preserve complementary signals.

application.claim: For multi-view anomaly detection systems, consider explicit disentanglement before combining representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works across datasets, anomaly types, or fusion architectures beyond the reported setting.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, and experimental conditions are not specified.
Quantitative results and ablation findings are not provided.
The abstract does not state limitations or independent verification of the reported effectiveness.
